assets.alt: Pipeline from code through build and test in continuous integration, then release, deploy, and operate in continuous delivery or deployment; production deployment may be manual or automatic.
assets.caption: CI validates code through build and test; CD carries a release toward production, manually or automatically.

assets.alt: AWS EC2 Create key pair dialog with a key-pair name, RSA selected, and PEM private-key format selected for OpenSSH.
assets.caption: An EC2 key pair provides the private credential needed for secure administrative access to the instance.

assets.alt: AWS VPC architecture where a public load balancer routes HTTPS, HTTP, and SSH target groups to one EC2 instance, with security groups restricting traffic by source address.
assets.caption: The load balancer exposes named endpoints while security groups restrict which traffic can reach the EC2 instance.

assets.alt: Google Cloud load-balancer details page showing an HTTPS frontend, a default routing rule, and a backend service with its health check and security policy.
assets.caption: A global application load balancer connects the public HTTPS frontend and routing rules to a health-checked backend service.

assets.alt: Google Cloud managed instance group form with autoscaling enabled, minimum and maximum instance counts, an HTTP load-balancing utilization target, and an initialization period.
assets.caption: Managed instance groups scale between explicit limits in response to a chosen utilization signal.

assets.alt: Google Cloud instance-group autohealing settings with a global TCP health check on port 443 and configured interval, timeout, healthy, and unhealthy thresholds.
assets.caption: Autohealing depends on a concrete health check whose interval, timeout, and thresholds define when an instance is replaced.

assets.alt: Three Git states showing files moving from the working directory to the staging area with git add and into the repository with git commit.
assets.caption: Git separates local edits, the staged snapshot, and committed history into three distinct states.

assets.alt: GitFlow branch diagram with main, develop, feature, release, and hotfix branches and their merge paths.
assets.caption: GitFlow uses long-lived main and develop branches, with short-lived feature, release, and hotfix branches.

assets.alt: Jenkins job page for payment-transactions-etl showing a red failed status and links to the last build, failed build, unsuccessful build, and completed build.
assets.caption: A failed Jenkins run is the starting point for diagnosis through build history and execution logs.

assets.alt: Jenkins job configuration with Build periodically enabled using a cron schedule and an Execute shell step that runs a Python ETL job.
assets.caption: A scheduled Jenkins job combines a cron trigger with a reproducible non-interactive command.

assets.alt: GitHub production-environment dialog for a pending deployment with a comment field and Reject or Approve and deploy actions.
assets.caption: A protected production environment inserts a human approval gate before deployment proceeds.

assets.alt: GitHub Open a pull request page comparing a feature branch with main and providing title, description, reviewer, assignee, label, and project fields.
assets.caption: A pull request packages a branch comparison with review context before changes reach the deployment branch.

assets.alt: GitHub Actions workflow running Terraform init, plan, and apply against an S3 remote-state bucket while a DynamoDB table acquires and releases state locks.
assets.caption: Remote state in S3 and locking in DynamoDB keep automated Terraform runs consistent and serialized.
